summary: Auric's opened luxury ring is shelter, not safety: refugees wake beneath chandeliers while longtime residents discover strangers occupying abandoned homes.
settingText: INT. AURIC BAZAAR — LUXURY RING CONCOURSE — MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: My parents' things are still in there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: We were told the rooms were empty.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Then where do her parents go?

panelPlan: Wide chandelier concourse converted into a crowded shelter.
A resident confronts Richard at her sealed family apartment.
Paul moves protectively between the adults.
Halev arrives as Dain refuses an easy eviction.
Both families remain on opposite sides of one doorway.
directionInline: Make the luxury ring feel like contested shelter rather than reclaimed housing: refugee bedding, old family possessions and civic staff should occupy the same doorway. No one is clearly wrong, and Halev's inability to promise where the resident family goes must remain visible.

summary: A shared heat failure forces two families into one room; Richard saves a resident child with medicine carried out of Tal Corvus.
settingText: INT. LUXURY RING — TEMPORARY APARTMENT

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Then tell me what she took.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Blue lips, shallow breathing. She's not fine.

panelPlan: Emergency lights and visible breath crowd both families together.
The resident child collapses.
Richard opens his last field kit.
Paul steadies the lamp while the mother holds her child.
The child breathes as the adults meet eyes without reconciliation.
directionInline: The medical emergency should interrupt the property dispute rather than resolve it. Richard uses refugee medicine on the resident child without asking for moral credit; the shared heat failure keeps both families dependent on the same failing room.

summary: Venn leaves for tribunal; Naomi believes the Fleet is withdrawing its most trustworthy person exactly when Auric needs her.
settingText: INT. AURIC DOCK — DEPARTURE GLASS

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: They take your ship and you still answer the summons.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: If I don't, Keating gets to explain why.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: We stay here with the damage while you go argue about it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I probably don't. Not all of it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Then come back with something useful.

panelPlan: Venn's escort shuttle waits beyond immense glass.
Naomi blocks Venn's path.
Their controlled anger closes the distance.
Venn almost reaches for Naomi and stops.
Venn boards while Naomi remains reflected beside the shuttle.
directionInline: Naomi's anger is about asymmetry of consequence, not abandonment. Keep the departing shuttle and Auric's damaged public space in the same visual field so Venn literally leaves the place Naomi must continue managing.

summary: Dominion frames Venn's tribunal as a clean command failure; Kerr forces the dead and saved back into the record.
settingText: INT. DAWNWARD HORIZON — ADMIRALTY TRIBUNAL — DAY

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Did you understand the withdrawal order?

dialogueInline.speaker: Keating
dialogueInline.text: And Billie Rusk escaped while you held fire.

dialogueInline.speaker: Keating
dialogueInline.text: Because your restraint left her able to.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kerr
dialogueInline.text: The civilians are alive because Venn went back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: This court is not weighing sentiment.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Then don't call the people who died 'sentiment.'

panelPlan: Venn stands alone below the circular Admiralty dais.
Keating projects Billie's escape and the damaged tug.
Dominion reduces the events to the order chain.
Kerr activates civilian testimony.
Venn faces accusation and survivors simultaneously.
directionInline: The tribunal architecture should make command hierarchy visually clean while Kerr's evidence makes the event morally messy. Civilian testimony and casualty records should intrude on the neat order-chain presentation rather than decorate it.

summary: Richard proves that Triarch policy selectively cut heat and medicine to disloyal districts, turning broader scarcity into targeted suffering that can be documented.
settingText: INT. AURIC LUXURY RING — IMPROVISED CLINIC

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: No. Somebody shut them down one at a time.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Clinic copies. Power logs. Official versions changed twice.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: If this leaves the room, they'll come for you.

panelPlan: Richard treats locals and refugees side by side.
He compares identical tissue damage across clinical records with district power and medicine shutdown logs.
Paul recognizes districts where official reports claimed unrelated shortages.
Tess sees the deliberate sequence in the timestamps.
Richard holds duplicated clinic and utility records as dangerous evidence, not a ceremonial archive object.
directionInline: Treat the discovery as forensic work: mismatched official reports, clinic copies, utility timestamps and district maps. The evidence proves selective punitive shutdowns inside broader scarcity; do not imply every shortage in the frontier was fabricated.

summary: Halev asks Auric to extend shelter; Dain makes him admit that Verge families will pay for the promise.
settingText: INT. AURIC BAZAAR — CIVIC CHAMBER

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: No one goes back to Tal Corvus.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Another section lost heat last night.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Finish that sentence and I'm putting your price sheet through the wall.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: My district is sleeping six to a room.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: What do you want me to say?

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Start with what we know. Then tell them what we can actually do.

panelPlan: The crowded chamber overlooks refugees beyond glass.
Halev asks for an extension.
Dain shows failing residential levels.
Wallace's market answer is rejected.
Naomi makes Halev name the harmed district.
directionInline: Sera should control the room by forcing costs into names and places. Keep the failing district map visible while Wallace offers a market abstraction and Naomi reacts too aggressively, allowing Sera—not Naomi—to define the civilian political question.

summary: Families forced together refuse to reduce one another to abstractions when a local child needs refugee care.
settingText: INT. LUXURY RING — WARMING ROOM

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: Were these rooms always this cold?

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: No. They used to be ugly and warm.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Lift her. Don't lay her flat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Want to see a light trick?

panelPlan: Families pack around one improvised heater.
The resident child struggles to breathe.
Refugees surrender blanket and space.
Paul distracts the frightened children while Richard works.
The resident mother makes room for Richard.
directionInline: This page is not reconciliation. The families cooperate because one child cannot breathe. Preserve guarded body language while blanket, space and medical attention move across the earlier social boundary.

summary: Public knowledge of Jex's passage turns refuge into a hunted commodity; Tali warns him to close the remaining network.
settingText: INT. VEIL MARKET — JEX'S OFFICE / TALI'S SAFEHOUSE

dialogueInline.speaker: Tali
dialogueInline.text: Three strangers asked for your passage by name.

panelPlan: Jex is surrounded by competing demands.
A private distorted-glass call resolves into Tali.
Her refuge quietly prepares to disappear.
Jex receives another plea from trapped families.
His hands hover between closing and accepting the route.
directionInline: Tali's refuge should look operational and vulnerable: packed bags, erased route marks and people preparing to move. Jex's hesitation must occur between two real groups of people who both need the same network.

summary: The Trade Mask offers restored trade for Richard's return, forcing Paul to ask whether one surrender could buy safety for everyone else.
settingText: INT. IMPROVISED CLINIC — BROADCAST LIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Trade Mask
dialogueInline.text: Return Richard Secundo. Reject Fleet occupation. Trade resumes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: If you go, do they leave Auric alone?

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Would you do it for me?

panelPlan: Clinic screens seize into a masked broadcast.
The Triarch promises restored trade and amnesty.
Richard is publicly labeled thief and traitor.
Paul studies his father while patients watch.
Richard kills the screen but cannot answer him.
directionInline: Introduce the Silent Triarch as a three-mask council while the Trade Mask alone speaks the offer. Raid and Fear remain silent in the background. The visual distinction between the masks should be readable without explanatory captions so later differences feel like an existing structure, not a retcon.

summary: Abby arrives alone with warning of Billie and Pike's gathering force; Auric must decide whether a disarmed Shard warlord may enter.
settingText: INT./EXT. AURIC SECURITY LOCK

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Billie's got captains with her. They want payback more than they want to live.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: I want you alive tomorrow. Hate me then.

panelPlan: Abby's tiny shuttle waits while Scythe remains distant.
She places her weapons in the lock tray.
Dain faces her through armored glass.
Abby shows Pike and Billie's gathering force.
Halev opens the door while Naomi remains ready.
directionInline: Abby earns entry by arriving physically alone and disarmed while her warship remains outside. Sera owns the political skepticism, Naomi owns the security risk, and Halev accepts personal responsibility for opening the door.

summary: Abby expects Tess, her sister, to return; Tess refuses to abandon people harmed by captains they once led.
settingText: INT. AURIC LUXURY RING — CLINIC PASSAGE

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Billie's gone. Pike went with her. Come home.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: My sister commanded people who did this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: You think staying here fixes it?

panelPlan: The sisters see each other across the crowded clinic.
Abby offers Tess her command token.
Tess continues dressing a civilian wound.
Abby absorbs the refusal.
The token remains on an empty cot between them.
directionInline: The sisters' history should sit in the unused command token between them. Tess keeps treating patients throughout the argument, making staying an action she is already performing rather than a declaration about who she has become.

summary: Kerr offers Venn a defensible lie; Venn insists the tribunal judge her actual rejection of Dominion's order.
settingText: INT. ADMIRALTY TRIBUNAL — RECESS ALCOVE

dialogueInline.speaker: Kerr
dialogueInline.text: Call it protection of Fleet strategic interests.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: That's not why I went back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kerr
dialogueInline.text: Say it your way and they'll use it before you're done talking.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Then they can do it on the record.

panelPlan: Venn and Kerr stand behind a translucent screen.
Kerr offers the prepared defense.
Venn deletes it.
Kerr warns her what honesty costs.
Venn returns without notes.
directionInline: Kerr's proposed defense should look genuinely useful, not cowardly. Venn deletes the argument because it is false, forcing the tribunal to judge the actual choice instead of allowing the scene to become a purity test.

summary: Keating freezes Fleet support to Auric, making Verge civilians bear part of the punishment for Venn's choice.
settingText: INT. AURIC ESCORT CONTROL / LUXURY RING

dialogueInline.speaker: Deka
dialogueInline.text: Commodore Venn doesn't command this ship anymore.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: And we went dark while she talked.

panelPlan: Naomi receives the withdrawal order.
Thunderbreak recedes beyond Auric jurisdiction.
The clinic loses a Fleet power feed.
Dain sees a shelter level go dark.
Naomi closes Venn's personal channel without calling.
directionInline: Show the withdrawal as material loss: a power feed goes dark, medical support disappears and Thunderbreak moves beyond the boundary. Sera and Naomi should experience the same act through different lenses—punishment and leverage.

summary: Richard agrees to independent testimony only if his evidence cannot authorize Fleet occupation and Paul may remain private.
settingText: INT. AURIC ARCHIVE BOOTH — NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Broadcasting from Auric paints the station around you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: The target was painted before I got here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Your conditions go on record first.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: No Fleet custody. And nobody gets to use my testimony to put troops here.

panelPlan: An independent evidence-and-broadcast booth waits dark: practical public-record infrastructure with a camera, source-file access, provenance checks, and tamper indicators rather than a ceremonial archive space.
Halev warns that a transmission from Auric makes the station a target.
Richard sets conditions limiting how his evidence may be used.
Paul refuses the seat beside him and Richard accepts the decision.
Dain activates the tamper-evident public feed and places Richard’s conditions at its beginning.
directionInline: The archive booth is ordinary evidence infrastructure. Richard's conditions must appear in the public record before his testimony begins, and Paul's refusal of the camera should be accepted without turning him into a symbolic witness.

summary: Richard names individual victims; testimony spreads because it refuses strategic abstraction.
settingText: INT. AURIC ARCHIVE / INTERCUT TAL CORVUS

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Nemi Vale. Six weeks old. Incubator power denied.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Ors Dane. Antibiotics withheld after his district protested.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Sergeant Pell carried medicine to children. They executed him for theft.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Then let him say their names.

dialogueInline.speaker: Another Listener
dialogueInline.text: Send it before they cut the channel.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: They called them shortages. The logs show who lost power and when.

panelPlan: Richard sits alone before the camera with source records visibly paired to the testimony feed so named people remain tied to specific clinical and policy evidence.
An infant’s clinical entry is paired with the remembered face of the patient Richard actually treated.
A Shard engine crew stops work to listen.
Paul hears familiar people and districts named outside the booth.
Anonymous hands retransmit the testimony and supporting data before authorities can suppress the channel.
directionInline: Keep names paired with source records and remembered faces so testimony never floats free of evidence. The spread of the feed should happen through ordinary workers retransmitting it, not through a grand public awakening.

summary: Billie accepts Pike's strike because Richard's truth makes Abby and Tess's rejection impossible to dismiss as weakness.
settingText: INT. BROKEN OATH — WAR ROOM

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: So that's it? A doctor with a camera decides who runs the Shards?

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: Abby ran. Tess is playing nurse. Now he gets to call it virtue.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pike
dialogueInline.text: Then give her somewhere she has to stand.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: No. Make them watch him fail.

panelPlan: Richard's testimony fills the battered display.
A named child's death affects Billie.
Pike overlays the Auric attack path.
Billie sees the clinic marker.
She takes the strike control key.
directionInline: Billie should react to one named victim before Pike turns the testimony into an attack opportunity. Her agreement to strike Auric is therefore a choice to answer uncomfortable truth with spectacle, not ignorance of what Richard said.

summary: Shard sleepers sabotage the luxury ring and plant Richard's insignia, turning residents against refugees as heat fails.
settingText: INT. LUXURY RING — HEAT EXCHANGE / CONCOURSE

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Not by a badge left where we'd find it.

panelPlan: A gloved hand destroys the exchanger and plants insignia.
Lights die across the concourse.
Residents find the planted evidence.
Accusation becomes a physical fight.
Richard places himself between Paul and the crowd.
directionInline: The planted insignia must look almost too convenient once Halev sees the physical damage. Let the crowd's fear become dangerous before officials can explain anything; Richard protecting Paul should precede any argument about evidence.

summary: Naomi forces Halev and Dain to tell everyone the ring may fail, choosing public trust over managed calm.
settingText: INT. AURIC CIVIC BROADCAST PLATFORM

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Say that now and people run.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: They're already running. They just don't know where.

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: The ring may not have one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: That we might lose the ring and we don't know when.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: The ring may not stay habitable.

panelPlan: The three argue while a crowd pounds the doors.
Halev asks for delay.
Dain demands evacuation.
Naomi activates the live feed mid-argument.
They face the frightened station together.
directionInline: Naomi should activate the broadcast while the leaders are still disagreeing, denying them the chance to polish a unified message. The public hears uncertainty and argument along with the evacuation warning.

summary: Halev and Dain surrender their own security before asking residents and refugees to share shelter.
settingText: INT. AURIC INNER SHELTER GATE

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Stop. Who told you to do that?

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: Where you were asking us to go.

panelPlan: Officials privilege registered residents.
Richard turns away with Paul.
Halev tears up his own authorization.
Dain gives away her family berth.
Mixed families enter while both leaders remain outside.
directionInline: Halev and Sera give up privileged access before asking anyone else to share. Their families and security remain unresolved outside the frame; the point is not martyrdom but removing an exemption they cannot ethically defend.

summary: Jex learns the public passage is watched; saving the ring requires exposing Tali's remaining private haven network.
settingText: INT. JEX'S OFFICE / TALI SAFEHOUSE / AURIC MAP

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Your famous passage is a firing gallery.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Want to try that answer again?

dialogueInline.speaker: Tali
dialogueInline.text: They'll find everybody if you don't.

panelPlan: The public passage is surrounded by hostile contacts.
Naomi asks for another way.
Jex reveals a faint hidden web.
Tali understands his consideration.
Her haven glows as one node among many.
directionInline: The hidden route network should be clearly larger than Jex's already-public passage. Tali's haven is one node among many, so opening the system saves Auric by exposing the people who made Jex's private advantage possible.

summary: Jex opens the private routes, saving the ring while Tali's refuge disappears from his board.
settingText: INT. JEX'S OFFICE / EXT. AURIC HIDDEN APERTURES

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Once I send this, there are no private doors.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tali
dialogueInline.text: There are people behind the public ones.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: I can protect the ships. Not every point they leave from.

panelPlan: Jex releases the authentication web.
Concealed apertures ignite around Auric.
Civilian craft emerge toward the ring.
Tali's node flashes exposed.
It goes black under Jex's hand.
directionInline: The route release should feel irreversible. As concealed apertures activate, Tali's node becomes visible and then disappears; Jex must keep transmitting even after he realizes the cost has become personal.

summary: Billie and Pike attack the evacuation; Billie drives toward Richard while civilians cross exposed spans.
settingText: EXT./INT. AURIC LUXURY RING — UNDER ATTACK

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: It was split before we got here.

panelPlan: Pike's force erupts through fractured ring light.
Evacuation craft scatter.
Billie drives Ashfang into the structure.
The clinic ceiling tears as Tess shields Richard and Paul.
Billie sees the clinic marker ahead.
directionInline: Keep the attack attached to the evacuation geometry. Billie and Pike are not simply attacking Auric; they are forcing civilians to cross exposed space while hunting Richard inside the same structure.

summary: Naomi accepts Abby's ships only under Verge command and only to protect civilians.
settingText: INT. AURIC ESCORT CONTROL / ABBY'S SHUTTLE

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: I've got six captains outside your line.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: They work for me inside the line. Civilians only. No chasing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: It's a shield job. Take it or don't.

panelPlan: Evacuation craft fill Naomi's displays.
Abby offers her remaining ships.
Naomi rejects broad command access.
She assigns civilian shield duty.
Abby relays the order to her defectors.
directionInline: Naomi accepts Abby's help only after narrowing its purpose to civilian protection. Abby's frustration should remain, but the tactical display must show her ships moving into the assigned shield positions rather than pursuing enemies.

summary: Verge escorts, Abby's defectors and Auric workers fight together while Thunderbreak watches beyond jurisdiction.
settingText: EXT. AURIC BAZAAR — RINGSPACE BATTLE

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Civilian Three, break toward the gold strut.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Thunderbreak, people are dying in front of you.

panelPlan: Escorts thread luminous ring architecture.
Abby's ships take fire for refugee craft.
Workers launch rescue skiffs by hand.
Thunderbreak holds beyond the boundary.
Deka watches a civilian ship tumble toward fire.
directionInline: The coalition should look improvised and unequal: Verge escorts, Abby's defectors, worker skiffs and Thunderbreak outside jurisdiction all solve different parts of the same emergency. No formation should suddenly look like a unified fleet.

summary: Dominion offers Venn restoration for withdrawal and Richard's transfer; Venn refuses and leaves her crew to choose.
settingText: INT. ADMIRALTY TRIBUNAL / THUNDERBREAK BRIDGE

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Resume command. Withdraw Thunderbreak. Transfer Secundo afterward.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: You're offering my ship for a doctor.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Then you have no order to give.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: He's right. I can't order you across.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: But you can see who's getting shot.

panelPlan: Battle footage fills the tribunal.
Dominion presents restoration orders.
Venn leaves them untouched.
Her unauthorized channel reaches Thunderbreak.
Deka advances the ship across the boundary.
directionInline: Dominion's offer must be visibly attractive: command restored, legal authority returned, a route out of chaos. Venn refuses the bargain and then deliberately stops short of issuing an unlawful order, leaving Deka's crossing as the crew's choice.

summary: Billie reaches Richard's clinic; Tess finally stops the woman she kept calling family.
settingText: INT. LUXURY RING — CLINIC PRESSURE CORRIDOR

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Funny. Strangers get the loyal version.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I kept calling you family so I wouldn't have to stop you.

panelPlan: Billie enters through smoke.
Tess blocks the corridor.
Their shared Shard history is visible.
Close combat ruptures the pressure window.
Billie bleeds beside the buckling barrier.
directionInline: The fight must read as intimacy turned physical. Billie and Tess know each other's habits, but Tess is no longer using that familiarity to excuse her. Pressure damage around them keeps the fight dangerous to everyone nearby.

summary: Richard treats Billie while Pike abandons her; Billie refuses Abby's offered rescue.
settingText: INT./EXT. CLINIC BREACH / AURIC RING

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: You don't get to pick that for me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: She came here to kill you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: No, he won't. Take my hand.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: So you get to forgive me?

panelPlan: Richard clamps Billie's wound.
Tess holds the failing pressure barrier.
Pike turns from Billie's distress beacon.
Abby reaches with an offered hand.
Billie escapes alone in an emergency launch.
directionInline: Richard treats Billie while Paul objects, preserving the medical ethic that has defined him since Mercy of Dawn. Abby's offered hand is rescue without forgiveness; Billie's refusal keeps her outside reconciliation.

summary: The coalition saves Auric, but every faction emerges altered and no one owns the victory.
settingText: INT./EXT. AURIC BAZAAR — AFTERMATH

dialogueInline.speaker: Kerr
dialogueInline.text: The finding is removal from command.

panelPlan: Incompatible ships hold amid debris.
Locals and refugees carry wounded together.
Dain and Halev reopen shared shelter.
Abby watches Tess remain at the clinic.
Venn hears the guilty finding as testimony spreads behind her.
directionInline: Do not stage the aftermath as a victory tableau. Each faction has lost something: Venn command, Abby unity, Tess family certainty, Auric infrastructure. The meaningful success is that civilians and evidence survived.

summary: Auric accepts refugees, rejects permanent Fleet jurisdiction, and founds an unauthorized defense compact; Tali is missing.
settingText: INT. AURIC CIVIC CHAMBER / JEX'S OFFICE

dialogueInline.speaker: Sera
dialogueInline.text: If all we're offering is a bunk, this is a waiting room.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: And nobody who leaves us gets claimed back by the Shards.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Nobody who testified gets handed back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: We call each other. We show up.

panelPlan: A mixed public chamber reconvenes.
Dain enters the shelter guarantee.
Halev strikes permanent Fleet authority.
The principals assent to mutual civilian defense.
Jex receives TALI STATUS UNKNOWN.
directionInline: The compact should emerge as a list of limits and obligations rather than a triumphant constitution. Jex's Tali alert should intrude at the end, making the new public order coexist with a private unresolved cost.

summary: Under Fleet detention, Venn learns the compact exists without authorization; she and Naomi acknowledge what lies between them.
settingText: INT. FLEET DETENTION TRANSIT / AURIC OBSERVATION GLASS

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Agreed not to be in charge. Nearly killed her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Unofficial things are hard to kill.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Come back and make it worse.

panelPlan: Venn sits in a spare transit compartment without insignia.
Naomi stands against Auric observation glass.
Their permitted call connects.
Their hands align on opposite screens without touching.
Incompatible ships guard the shared shelter lights.
directionInline: Keep Venn's detention visible throughout the call: no insignia, restricted compartment, permitted connection. Naomi's invitation is affectionate but not absolution; the final image of incompatible ships guarding the same shelter should carry the larger promise.
